# Unit test for function is_multiply_prime
def test_is_multiply_prime():
    # Product of three distinct primes
    assert is_multiply_prime(30) == True   # 2 * 3 * 5
    assert is_multiply_prime(70) == True   # 2 * 5 * 7
    assert is_multiply_prime(105) == True  # 3 * 5 * 7

    # Product with repeated primes
    assert is_multiply_prime(8) == True    # 2 * 2 * 2
    assert is_multiply_prime(12) == True   # 2 * 2 * 3
    assert is_multiply_prime(27) == True   # 3 * 3 * 3
    assert is_multiply_prime(125) == True  # 5 * 5 * 5

    # Single primes are not a product of three primes
    assert is_multiply_prime(2) == False
    assert is_multiply_prime(5) == False
    assert is_multiply_prime(97) == False

    # Product of only two primes
    assert is_multiply_prime(4) == False   # 2 * 2
    assert is_multiply_prime(6) == False   # 2 * 3
    assert is_multiply_prime(15) == False  # 3 * 5

    # Product of four primes
    assert is_multiply_prime(16) == False  # 2 * 2 * 2 * 2
    assert is_multiply_prime(24) == False  # 2 * 2 * 2 * 3

    # Trivial / edge cases
    assert is_multiply_prime(0) == False
    assert is_multiply_prime(1) == False
    assert is_multiply_prime(-30) == False

    # Boundary: largest product of three primes within loop range
    assert is_multiply_prime(97 * 97 * 97) == True  # 912673

    # Prime factor outside the search range (101 > 100 is never checked)
    assert is_multiply_prime(2 * 101 * 101) == False

test_is_multiply_prime()
print("All tests passed!")
